text:
tom: FYI customer (acme-corp) opened a support ticket — p99 token latency jumped from ~120ms to 900ms-1.2s for a few minutes. They claim requests are routed AP-SOUTH-1 but traces show an EU hop. Correlation ID: corr-9a7b2f. Started ~2026-03-16 11:02 UTC. Anyone seen region bounce like this? :eyes:
sara: Can you paste a traceroute + the minimal request they used? Also need the full route-decision log for corr-9a7b2f.
tom: Pasting what customer provided: 
```
$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate?model=redwood/fast-l2&input=hello"
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (13.32.45.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate?model=redwood/fast-l2&input=hello HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.com
> Authorization: Bearer sk-...
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-corr-id: corr-9a7b2f
< x-route: ap-proxy-02 -> eu-edge-01 -> model-srv-34
< latency-ms: 972
```
And traceroute from their client:
```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.com (13.32.45.12), 30 hops max
 1  client-gw (10.0.0.1)  0.5 ms  0.6 ms  0.4 ms
 2  ap-edge-01.redwood (13.225.11.5)  12.2 ms  12.0 ms  11.8 ms
 3  ap-proxy-02.redwood (13.225.12.9)  13.1 ms  13.0 ms  12.9 ms
 4  eu-peering-01 (18.204.3.19)  220.7 ms  221.0 ms  220.9 ms
 5  eu-edge-01.redwood (3.121.44.2)  221.8 ms  222.0 ms  221.6 ms
 6  model-srv-34 (10.2.3.45)  222.3 ms  221.9 ms  222.1 ms
```
Note hop 4 is unexpected — peering to EU from AP.

priya: I pulled the route-decisions for corr-9a7b2f from the routing service: 
``time=2026-03-16T11:02:03Z corr=corr-9a7b2f src_region=ap-south-1 route_decision=EU_FALLBACK reason=capacity_threshold_crossed selected_endpoint=eu-edge-01``
There was a rapid capacity spike on ap-proxy pool and the policy `prefer_eu_on_burst: true` kicked in. We're seeing the autoscale cooldown behave incorrectly — it marked AP pool as unhealthy for 180s even though nodes were still up.

luis: That policy was added last quarter for cost controls, but we never expected it to trigger for short-lived bursts. We should revert the policy or tighten the trigger. For now, workaround is to force region preference via request header or pin model replica.
mike: Quick repro steps for support to run against their client: 
1) Run curl with header `X-Region-Preference: ap-south-1`
2) If still hit EU, run with `?trace=1` to get the full route trace back.
Example: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "X-Region-Preference: ap-south-1" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate?model=redwood/fast-l2&input=hi&trace=1"
```
If server responds with `x-route: ap-proxy -> eu-edge` then collect tcpdump on ap-proxy: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 13.32.45.12 -w /tmp/ap-proxy.pcap` and attach.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260316-41 assigned -> eng-runtime, eng-sre (priority: P2) :rotating_light:

priya: I'm opening a config rollback PR to disable `prefer_eu_on_burst` and reducing the unhealthy timeout from 180s -> 15s. If that lands quickly it should stop the accidental EU failovers.

sara: For support response to the customer: ask them to retry with header `X-Route-Force: ap-south-1` and collect `trace=1` output. Offer to pin a dedicated ap pool for their tenant while we fix the policy.

tom: FYI I told the customer the temporary workaround (header pin) and asked for the pcap and trace. Also let them know we're investigating the autoscale policy and will follow up in incident INC-20260316-41. :thumbsup:

luis: After PR lands, I'll watch P99 for AP-SOUTH-1 and check for any residual stickiness. Will also add a regression test to prevent `prefer_eu_on_burst` from triggering for bursts < 5s.

mike: Note for eng-runtime: route logs show `decision_stack=[latency_estimate, capacity_metric, cost_acl]` — the cost_acl was evaluating higher weight than regional affinity during this event. We should adjust weights.

sara: OK, assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime -> tweak weight + regression; eng-sre -> monitor and validate rollback; support -> collect customer artifacts and send workaround.

tom: Closing loop here once we have pcap + trace or PR merged. Thanks all.
